title: PhysxAutoDeformableAttachmentAPI
summary: An authoring container that generates vertex attachments and element collision filters between its two attachables, a deformable body and a second deformable body or an Xformable's colliders. The runtime finds it by the applied API at load; on an ovstage attach the attachment and filter children are generated in memory and their data is computed from these columns.
producer_scope: Published like any applied physics API: every declared attribute at its resolved value, relationships only when authored; a prim carrying this API is in physics scope on its own. No column is rewritten or created by the producer.

columns.name: physxAutoDeformableAttachment:attachable0
columns.absent: No attachment: both attachable relationships must exist with exactly one target each, otherwise attachable parsing fails with a warning and nothing is generated. A target is a deformable body (OmniPhysicsDeformableBodyAPI) or an Xformable whose colliders are used; supported pairs are volume-volume, volume-surface and deformable-Xformable, in either order.

columns.name: physxAutoDeformableAttachment:attachable1
columns.absent: Same as attachable0: without exactly one target on each relationship nothing is generated.

columns.name: physxAutoDeformableAttachment:collisionFilteringOffset
columns.absent: 0: elements are filtered only where they overlap the other actor. A non-finite value (the schema fallback -inf) selects the heuristic, 10% of the smaller average dimension of the two actors, so write the value you mean.

columns.name: physxAutoDeformableAttachment:deformableVertexOverlapOffset
columns.absent: 0: a deformable vertex is attached only where it lies inside the other actor.

columns.name: physxAutoDeformableAttachment:enableCollisionFiltering
columns.absent: false: no collision filtering is computed and the generated filter children are published disabled. USD's fallback is true, so write the value.

columns.name: physxAutoDeformableAttachment:enableDeformableFilteringPairs
columns.absent: false: between two deformable bodies every overlapping element of one is filtered against every overlapping element of the other, instead of per overlapping element pair. Not used with an Xformable attachable.

columns.name: physxAutoDeformableAttachment:enableDeformableVertexAttachments
columns.absent: false: no vertex attachments are computed and the generated attachment children are published disabled. USD's fallback is true, so write the value.

columns.name: physxAutoDeformableAttachment:enableRigidSurfaceAttachments
columns.absent: false. The flag has no effect in this runtime: rigid surface sampling is compiled out, so the value only enters the attachment input CRC.

columns.name: physxAutoDeformableAttachment:maskShapes
columns.absent: No mask: every vertex and element is a candidate. Sphere, Cube and Capsule targets restrict attachments to points inside them (filtering to points within collisionFilteringOffset of them); other targets are ignored.

columns.name: physxAutoDeformableAttachment:rigidSurfaceSamplingDistance
columns.absent: 0. The value has no effect in this runtime (rigid surface sampling is compiled out); it only enters the attachment input CRC, so the schema fallback -inf and an omitted column generate the same attachment.

interactions.rule: An attachable carrying OmniPhysicsDeformableBodyAPI is re-parsed as a deformable body (and auto-cooked when it enables PhysxAutoDeformableBodyAPI generation) before the attachment data is computed.

notes: The parameters are read when the attachment is set up or refreshed at load; the runtime does not watch them for live changes, and a refresh recomputes the data only when the input CRC over the parameters, the mask shapes and the attachables' cooked mesh data changed.

With a stage the runtime can author, the input CRC is stored in and read back from physxAutoDeformableAttachment:inputCrc, a runtime bookkeeping attribute no schema declares; on an ovstage attach it is kept in memory. It is not described here.
